vllm_recipe.content_summary: A DEDICATED but CPU-only recipe: 'Qwen3-8B is a dense Qwen3 model with hybrid thinking and non-thinking modes. This recipe includes an Intel Xeon 6 CPU configuration validated with BF16 serving.' Prerequisites: 2x Xeon 6 CPUs, vLLM >= 0.8.5. Launch command: 'vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8' (CPU path; the --gpu-memory-utilization flag name is retained by vLLM's CPU backend for a different resource-budget purpose). Docker variant uses image vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64 with '--tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3'. No GPU-specific section exists in this recipe.

weight_layout_evidence.note: The repository stores the SAME BF16 12.25B-parameter weights in TWO redundant formats: a single-file 'consolidated.safetensors' (24,495,604,224 bytes, ~22.8 GiB) for Mistral's own inference stack, AND a standard 5-shard HF-sharded set (model-00001..00005-of-00005.safetensors, summing to approximately the same ~22.8 GiB) for transformers/vLLM. usedStorage (49.04 GB) reflects both formats combined, not a single ~45GB weight set -- the actual model is ~22.8 GiB in either format, matching the registry's bf16_gb=24.5 figure closely (24.5 GB vs 22.8 GiB, consistent within GB/GiB unit rounding).
